name: Manchado
summary: A rare Argentine pattern: broad clean white over the back, crest and croup with smooth rounded islands of the base colour left inside it, a mostly white tail, and a dark head, belly and lower legs. Held here as a made-up recessive allele: two copies to show, so it can appear from two plain parents. That follows the leading idea in Sponenberg and Bellone's Equine Color Genetics (2017), a very rare recessive, but it is unproven - no gene, locus, variant, DNA test or OMIA entry exists, no pedigree study or genome-wide study has been published, and a somatic or other unusual cause has not been ruled out. Its own locus: it is not tobiano, sabino, splashed white or the leopard complex. Reported in a few horses, almost all in Argentina, among Criollos, Thoroughbreds, Arabians, polo ponies and Hackneys. No known effect on build, speed, hearing or sight.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two ordinary copies. Nothing shows and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: Manchado carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of ma. The horse is completely ordinary and there is no way to see it - but half its foals inherit the copy, and two carriers bred together are the only way manchado appears at all.

phenotypes.name: Manchado
phenotypes.description: Broad, clean white over the back, crest, shoulder and croup, with smooth rounded islands of the base colour left inside it and a mostly white tail. The head, the underside of the neck, the belly and the lower legs stay coloured - the pattern is top-down, which is what separates it from splash.
